pairs.subject: rate-limiting
pairs.evidence: src/components/modules/project-setup/BidirectionalStateSyncPanel/useBidirectionalStateSyncPanel.ts:78 This context is a browser-side panel. Each write is one operator click sent to the operator's own UE editor over the bridge WebSocket. It exposes no door that outside actors can drive and paces no third-party quota, so the precondition for a rate limit (bounding how much work a key may cause per unit of time) does not hold. A case-insensitive search of both panel directories for ratelimit, rate-limit, throttle, retry-after, 429 and tokenbucket found no hits.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/project-setup/LiveStateSyncPanel/PropertyWatchForm.tsx:48 This is the only timing number in the context. It is a watch sampling interval sent to UE, not a per-key admission window, so no limiter algorithm is being chosen here.

src/components/modules/project-setup/BidirectionalStateSyncPanel/useBidirectionalStateSyncPanel.ts:52 The only negative outcome is a frame dropped because the socket is closed. That is a transport failure, not a limiter refusal, and it is labelled as a drop. No rate-limit refusal is ever issued.
src/components/modules/project-setup/BidirectionalStateSyncPanel/constants.ts:4 The display log has a cap, but there is no refusal branch whose log volume needs managing.

src/components/modules/project-setup/BidirectionalStateSyncPanel/useBidirectionalStateSyncPanel.ts:94 PIE control goes straight from one local operator to their own editor. There is no population of actors competing for a resource, so there is nothing to key on.
